description: i017 (io-uring-sq-ring, snapshots/s04) complete. One reported finding: io_uring/uring_cmd.c:65-77 (io_uring_cmd_prep_async) performs memcpy(req->async_data, ioucmd->cmd, cmd_size) at line 75 from ioucmd->cmd, which io_uring_cmd_prep set at uring_cmd.c:101 to the raw inline sqe->cmd array in the user-mapped SQ ring (ctx->sq_sqes, io_uring.c:2410). The payload is first consumed live by file->f_op->uring_cmd(ioucmd, ...) at uring_cmd.c:133 and then independently re-fetched by the memcpy on the -EAGAIN retry path, with the retry executing from the second copy (uring_cmd.c:130-131); no READ_ONCE, local snapshot, or lock protects the shared bytes, exactly violating the seed's single-fetch invariant (documented in io_get_sqe's own comment at io_uring.c:2385-2391). Scalar fields (flags, buf_index, cmd_op) are READ_ONCE-cached in prep, so exposure is limited to the variable-length cmd[] payload; concrete driver-level OOB impact is unproven (medium confidence). Counterevidence/negative results: io_get_sqe (io_uring.c:2405) and fdinfo.c:92 both single-fetch the SQ array index and bounds-check the cached local (correct reference pattern); net.c:263 and net.c:999 read sqe->addr2/file_index only for rejection and never re-consume; kbuf.c:148 io_ring_buffer_select reads each provided-buffer field once with immediate use. Bounded limitations: only io_uring/ in s04 audited plus a scripted scan of all io_uring/*.c for repeated sqe-> field fetches; ->uring_cmd driver consumers (block/NVMe/SCSI/UBLK) not audited; other prep_async memcpy-from-SQE paths not exhaustively enumerated.
